description: Personal-detail screening policy shared by lib.py, convex/lib/agentIntake.ts and pow-cli. Every string value and every undeclared object key of an outgoing record is screened for phone numbers, email addresses and honorific-led names, whatever its schema says. Any 40- or 64-digit hex token (a maximal run of ASCII letters and digits, compared without regard to case) is refused wherever it appears, including inside longer text, unless the whole value of a designated hash field below is that digest, since a hash of a personal detail is itself a pseudonymous personal detail. Paths join object keys with dots and write every array index as []. Each designated field states its provenance: 'recomputed' fields are recomputed from their inputs in the same record and refused on mismatch; 'server_lookup' fields must name a stored object the backend finds before accepting the record; 'private_input' fields are digests of bytes the record does not carry (the operator's raw trace, prompt, instruction or definition text, or a source revision), kept in the private run directory or the repository, and are accepted on the operator's attestation because they cannot be recomputed here. The internal cited-name exception is defined in cited_name_rules.

public_source_cited.v1.description: A rule item names one exact code-point span in one of the four claim fields of its claim. The detected name must use strict ASCII token spacing and boundaries, and its ASCII-lowercase key must occur at bounded positions in the claim quotation. A valid rule item admits recurrences of that key only inside claim fields. Other dossier fields, object keys, review text, manifests, phones, emails, and first-pass records retain their existing refusal rules.
